name: Heart Rate
notes: Athletes may normally have 40-60 bpm. Fever increases HR by 10 bpm per 1 degree C. Newborns 120-160, infants 80-140, children 70-120.

name: SpO2 (Oxygen Saturation)
warning_range: 91-94% — concerning, requires monitoring and possible oxygen
critical_range: 90% or below — medical emergency, requires immediate oxygen support
notes: SpO2 below 90% is a medical emergency. COVID-19 patients may have silent hypoxia (low SpO2 without feeling breathless). Measure on fingertip without nail polish.

name: Body Temperature
warning_range: 37.3 to 38.9 degrees Celsius (fever) OR 35.0 to 36.0 degrees Celsius (mild hypothermia)
critical_range: Above 40.0 degrees Celsius (high fever) OR below 35.0 degrees Celsius (hypothermia)
notes: Temperature above 40C in adults is a medical emergency. In children above 38C warrants doctor visit. Oral temperature is 0.3-0.6C lower than rectal. Ear and forehead thermometers are less accurate.

name: Blood Pressure Systolic
critical_range: Above 180 mmHg (hypertensive crisis) OR below 80 mmHg (hypotension or shock)
notes: BP above 180 systolic is hypertensive emergency requiring immediate care. BP below 90 systolic with symptoms (dizziness, fainting, confusion) indicates shock. Always take 2-3 readings.

name: Blood Pressure Diastolic
notes: Diastolic above 120 with symptoms is hypertensive emergency. Pulse pressure (systolic minus diastolic) should normally be 40-60 mmHg.

name: Blood Glucose Fasting
critical_range: Below 54 mg/dL (severe hypoglycaemia — give sugar immediately) OR above 300 mg/dL (hyperglycaemic crisis)
notes: Fasting means 8 hours without food. Severe hypoglycaemia (below 54) needs immediate sugar intake. In known diabetics: below 70 requires fast-acting sugar (glucose tablets or juice). Above 250 with symptoms requires doctor.

name: Blood Glucose Random (Postprandial)
critical_range: Above 200 mg/dL (diabetes likely) OR above 400 mg/dL (hyperglycaemic emergency)
notes: Postprandial glucose measured 2 hours after starting a meal. Values above 200 on two separate occasions confirms diabetes diagnosis.

name: Respiratory Rate
warning_range: 21-25 breaths per minute (tachypnoea) OR 10-11 breaths per minute (bradypnoea)
critical_range: Above 30 breaths per minute OR below 8 breaths per minute
notes: Respiratory rate above 25 in an adult is a sign of respiratory distress. Count for a full 60 seconds. Normal in children: newborns 40-60, infants 30-60, toddlers 24-40, school age 18-30.
